reports_reviewed: VROSTBridge-Client-report_1.0.0.4_2026-10-07_19-04-54.json and its host report (the session without video)
VROSTBridge-Client-report_1.0.0.4_2026-10-07_21-09-20.json and its host report (10-bit colour off)
findings: Colour: the maintainer saw dark grey where the game is black on the Beyond 2e's OLED panels with 10-bit colour on, and black with it off. On the AMD path the 10-bit stream was converted by the encoder from 10-bit RGB, which gave studio-range samples (black at 64 of 1023) in a stream labelled full range.

No video: in the 19:04 session the client had no head pose from SteamVR in 75 of 92 samples (tracking results 101 and 100: calibrating), its video stayed at waiting_video and no frame arrived; the host renders only for a pose the client sends, so it dropped every frame without saying so.

Eye tracking: the eye-camera helper used about one processor core (median 101 % in the 10-second rows of the 21:09 session), decoding and encoding every picture again; eye-tracking samples swung between 10 and 55 a second; the gaze relay saw 11 pauses over a second, 5 over 5 seconds, the longest 10.1 s.

The sharp region: the maintainer could see it move. The host moved it whenever the gaze left a 2.5 % dead band, which the tracker's noise and small eye movements crossed every few frames (3.17 moves a second in a simulated minute of gaze).
Ultra: 3200 per eye on a Beyond, where SteamVR on the headset PC recommends 2712; the headset PC drew every frame at 3200.

Network: the 1.0.0.4 network test on the 1 Gbit/s USB Ethernet adapter found no clean rate (0.04 % packet loss and 3 frames at 80 Mbit/s; frames late from 150 Mbit/s by the time the companion read them; heavy loss from 400), so every later session ran at 30 Mbit/s with the result kept for 30 days. The evening before, the same adapter had carried 500 Mbit/s without loss.
changes: patches/0018-host-exact-colour-and-pose-drops.patch: on the AMD path the host converts RGB to Y'CbCr with a stated profile (BT.709 full range), converts a 128 x 64 test picture (black, white, red, mid grey) with the same converter at the start of every stream, reads the samples back, classifies range and matrix (VROSTBridgeColor.h) and labels the stream with what it measured (H.264 FULL_RANGE_COLOR, HEVC NOMINAL_RANGE, input and output colour profiles, AV1's); 8-bit when the check fails or the encoder refuses 10-bit; VROST_COLOR, VROST_COLOR_FALLBACK, VROST_COLOR_RELABEL, VROST_COLOR_CONVERTER lines; AV1 bitrate changes use AV1 properties; frames dropped without a head pose counted per 5 s (VROST_NO_HEAD_POSE)

patches/0019-host-gaze-comfort.patch: the gaze-driven region moves only when the gaze leaves gaze_comfort x half the region's size around its middle (default 0.5, 0 to 0.8, never below the 2.5 % dead band)

host/stream_options.py: gaze_comfort written only for a driver whose build manifest lists patch 0019 (feature gaze-comfort); host/events.py and launcher/app.py: the colour and pose-drop lines read into the session's telemetry and reports

client/device/openvr_device.cpp, client/platform/linux/main.cpp, client/ui/status_card.cpp, launcher/game_ui.py, launcher/desktop.html: head poses sent and missing and SteamVR's tracking result counted; Headset not tracked after 2 s (page, Game Mode, headset card); the host page says Waiting for the headset's position

client/device/conversion.hpp shownEyeSize, client/platform/linux/video.hpp: a stream larger than SteamVR's recommended size is shown at that size; client/platform/linux/vulkan.cpp: the decoder's colour logged when it changes; the page shows bit depth, range, the shown size and a note when 10-bit was asked for but the host streams 8-bit

third_party/go-bsb-cams (main.go, jpeg_frames.go, camera_stats.go, vendored go-uvc: isochronous_reader.go, bulk_reader.go, frame.go, claim_interval.go, uvc.go): pictures passed on as the cameras sent them (checked; standard Huffman tables added; one in 120 decoded in full), the fastest frame interval, damaged pictures skipped, reads and whole frames bounded in time, a clean reopen after 2 s without a picture, transfers of at most 32 packets, STATS and CAMERA lines, at most one picture per 8 ms per reader

launcher/eye_tracking.py, launcher/timeline.py: the helper's lines kept as values (cameras.feed, camera lines), camera pictures a second, losses and re-openings in the timeline; launcher/baballonia.py: the eye filter 2 Hz and 60 where it is still Baballonia's or 1.0.0.3's

launcher/link_test.py, launcher/network_test.py, launcher/app.py: kernel arrival times and the socket's own drops on Linux, credited to the steps they were sent in; a 0.5 ms thread switch interval while receiving; a warm-up step; frames after the last one seen in a step without an end marker counted from the host's summary; the pace limit from steady loss (1 %); a wired automatic bitrate of at most 40 % of the pace; a result without a clean rate tested again before the next session, up to three in a row, keeping an earlier clean result that is still young enough
launcher/graphics_limit.py: Set the GPU clock to automatic offered with the graphics warning for a GPU held at a fixed clock
Version 1.0.0.5 on both programs; documents and release notes
review: An independent review of the camera helper, patch 0018 and the network test found five defects, each fixed and covered by a test before these packages were built: a frame read that never returned while USB data kept coming without a frame; drops at a step's end credited to the next step, hiding its network loss; a libusb context kept for every unplug; a crash on a malformed USB packet header; an earlier network result kept although too old to be used. It found no defect in patch 0018.
